set_color.description: Set every zone to one HSBK colour — LightSetColor. Per-zone control needs the multizone family (SetColorZones, 501) instead.
set_color.notes: Message type 102. The payload is a reserved byte, the 8-byte HSBK, then duration — see the `hsbk` and `set_color` payload formats. Full red is hue 0, saturation and brightness 65535, kelvin 3500.

hue.description: Hue as a fraction of 360° across the full u16 range.

kelvin.description: White point; meaningful when saturation is 0.

saturation.description: 0 is white, in which case `kelvin` sets the white point.

turn_off.description: Turn the strip off — LightSetPower with level at zero.

duration.description: Fade time in milliseconds; 0 is instant.

turn_on.description: Turn the strip on — LightSetPower with level at full.
turn_on.notes: Message type 117. Light-level power, not the device-level SetPower (21).

duration.description: Fade time in milliseconds; 0 is instant.

device.name: LIFX Z
device.notes:
LIFX Z LED strips support the LIFX binary LAN protocol over UDP port 56700 with no authentication. The observed strips advertise HomeKit HAP over mDNS with md=LIFX Z; consumers can resolve IP address from mDNS and then send a UDP GetService message to port 56700 for full LIFX metadata. LIFX Z is a multizone light strip; common units expose eight zones using HSBK color. The current schema does not have a native UDP endpoint type, so protocol details are captured in protocol_handler and lifx_lan_protocol.
MATTER CAVEAT: LIFX's Matter firmware rollout (Sept 2025) is eligible on LCM3-edition hardware (firmware v3.x) only — the original LIFX Z (firmware v2.x) is excluded — and updating to Matter DECOMMISSIONS the HomeKit/HAP integration. Units that take the Matter update stop advertising _hap._tcp.local., which kills the mDNS discovery signal this spec relies on; discover those units by UDP broadcast GetService instead. The current vendor app bundles a Matter commissioning stack (its onboarding code carries a Matter path), which is the onboarding path it offers for Matter-firmware units.

credentials.notes: The legacy SetAccessPoint message carries the passphrase in plaintext; the setup AP itself is the only transport protection, and on the strips it is open. Post-setup LAN control is unauthenticated UDP on port 56700, so no client credential is issued and anything on the LAN can drive the strip.

factory_reset.effect: Clears WiFi credentials and returns the device to its unprovisioned, AP-hosting state.

procedures.indicator: The light cycles colours to confirm the reset.
procedures.name: Five power cycles

steps.action: Switch the fixture off and on five times, leaving it on for about two seconds each time.
Wait for the colour-cycle confirmation, then look for the setup AP.

methods.description: Join the device's own setup AP and drive the deprecated access-point messages over UDP 56700: confirm the device answers discovery, ask it to scan (GetAccessPoints), pick a network from the StateAccessPoint replies, and hand over credentials (SetAccessPoint with interface = STATION). The device then drops its AP and joins the home network. Send requests to the subnet broadcast address (255.255.255.255 works too) with unicast to gateway_ip as the fallback — original firmware answers discovery sent broadcast. On post-original hardware the vendor app uses the TLS TCP flow in the next method instead; whether these UDP messages still answer on newer firmware is untested.

get_access_point.description: Type 0x133 (307). Asks the device for the AP configuration currently set on one interface. 1-byte payload: interface (same encoding as SetAccessPoint). Present in the vendor app; not in the legacy public docs.

get_access_points.description: Type 0x130 (304). No payload. The device answers with one StateAccessPoint (0x132) message per network it can see. The full access-point family in the vendor app runs 304-309; 307-309 are documented after 306 below.

legacy_header.description: The 36-byte header the legacy access-point messages ride in, all little-endian. It is offset-compatible with the current LAN-protocol header — size at 0, protocol at 2, message type at 32 — and the fields between differ but are safe to send as zero: the modern source/sequence slots land where the legacy format put reserved bytes, the site MAC and a timestamp, and legacy firmware does not validate them.

fields.description: Total packet length, header plus payload.
fields.name: size

fields.description: 0x3400 for a broadcast/tagged request (discovery, and the setup exchange, where the target is unknown); 0x1400 when addressing one device. The same two constants the current protocol produces from its origin/tagged/addressable bits.
fields.name: protocol

fields.description: Legacy: always 0. Current firmware reads a client-chosen source id here; 0 is accepted and answered broadcast.
fields.name: reserved_source

fields.description: Device MAC (6 bytes) plus 2 zero bytes; all zero for broadcast.
fields.name: target

fields.description: Legacy site/gateway MAC; zero on requests.
fields.name: reserved_site

fields.description: Legacy: always 0. Current firmware reads ack/res flags and a sequence number here; zero asks for nothing extra.
fields.name: reserved_flags

security_protocols.description: The SECURITY_PROTOCOL byte shared by SetAccessPoint and StateAccessPoint.
security_protocols.notes: When the target network never appeared in a scan (hidden SSID, or a device that answers GetAccessPoints with nothing), WPA2_AES_PSK (5) is the value to try first — it is what home networks overwhelmingly run.

values.2: WEP_PSK (documented as not supported for joining)

set_access_point.description: Type 0x131 (305). Hands the device its home network. 98-byte payload; strings are UTF-8, null-padded to their fixed width. Layout confirmed byte-exact against the vendor app (interface at 0, ssid at 1, password at 33, security_protocol at 97).

fields.description: 1 = SOFT_AP, 2 = STATION. Send 2: the device's station interface is the one that joins the home network.
fields.name: interface

fields.description: Target network name, exactly as the device reported it when it came from GetAccessPoints.
fields.name: ssid

fields.description: Plaintext passphrase. The legacy exchange has no credential encryption; the setup AP is the only transport protection.
fields.name: password

fields.description: See security_protocols below. WEP networks are documented as not supported.
fields.name: security_protocol

set_access_point_broadcast.description: Type 0x135 (309). SetAccessPoint plus a trailing 16-byte key, 114-byte payload: interface (1 byte at 0), ssid (32 bytes at 1), password (64 bytes at 33), security_protocol (1 byte at 97), key (16 bytes at 98). Present in the vendor app; the key's purpose is not established.

state_access_point.description: Type 0x132 (306). One scan result. 38-byte payload. Layout confirmed byte-exact against the vendor app.

state_access_point_config.description: Type 0x134 (308). The device's currently configured AP, NOT a scan result (that is 306 above). 66-byte payload: interface (1 byte at 0), ssid (32-byte UTF-8 string at 1), passphrase (32 raw bytes at 33), security_protocol (1 byte at 65). Present in the vendor app; not replayed against hardware.

softap.port_notes: The same port as normal control: in setup mode the device is at gateway_ip on its own 172.16.0.0/24 subnet.
softap.ssid_notes: Post-original devices (LIFX Z among them) advertise an OPEN AP named after the product and a serial fragment. The vendor app confirms it: the app supplies a passphrase only when the setup SSID is exactly "LIFX Bulb" — the original 2013 bulbs, whose published passphrase is "lifx1234" — and joins every other LIFX-prefixed setup AP with none. open_network above therefore describes the strips this spec covers, and that constant is the fallback for the one older AP name.

Confirm the device answers on the setup network.

steps.expect: One StateAccessPoint (type 0x132) datagram per visible network; collect for scan_collect_seconds.
No reply is guaranteed. The setup AP drops within join_wait_seconds as the device joins the home network.

timing.join_wait_notes: After SetAccessPoint the device reboots its radio: its AP disappears and it joins the home network. There is no status-poll counterpart to Wemo's GetNetworkStatus — the confirmation is the device turning up on the home LAN.
timing.scan_collect_notes: StateAccessPoint replies arrive as separate datagrams over a few seconds; collect until quiet rather than after the first.

causes: The client fell back to cellular or another interface. Pin traffic to the 172.16.0.0/24 interface.
Broadcast datagrams are being dropped. Retry unicast to 172.16.0.1.

Post-original firmware: the vendor app onboards over TLS TCP to 172.16.0.1:56700 (next method), and Matter units via its bundled Matter stack. Whether these UDP messages still answer on newer firmware is untested.
troubleshooting.symptom: Nothing answers discovery on the setup AP.

causes: Some firmware scans lazily. Ask again after a few seconds, or skip the scan and send SetAccessPoint with a manually-entered SSID and WPA2_AES_PSK.
troubleshooting.symptom: GetAccessPoints returns nothing but discovery answers.

causes: Wrong passphrase, or a WEP or WPA3-only network. The legacy radio wants WPA/WPA2.
5 GHz-only SSID. The radio is 2.4 GHz.
Reset and retry; the exchange is fire-and-forget and a lost datagram fails silently.

methods.description: Modern flow, derived from the vendor app (app-derived, not hardware-verified — medium confidence). After joining the setup AP, the app opens a TLS-secured TCP connection to 172.16.0.1:56700 and drives the SAME LIFX binary access-point messages (304-309, layouts above) over the stream. The TLS handshake is mutual — the client presents key material bundled in the app — so a third-party client cannot complete it without that key material. Hardware hosting the original "LIFX Bulb" setup SSID is detected by name and gets a plaintext TCP connection to the same port instead. The schema has no softAP-binary-over-TCP method type, so this entry rides under softap_udp, but the transport here is TLS over TCP, not UDP.

softap.port_notes: TCP on this flow, unlike the legacy method: the same 56700 port number, TLS-wrapped on post-original hardware.

steps.action: Factory reset the strip (or power a new one) and wait for its setup AP.
steps.expect: An open AP named with the LIFX prefix appears; the device sits at 172.16.0.1 on it.

steps.action: Join the setup AP from the provisioning client.
Open a TLS TCP connection to 172.16.0.1:56700 (mutual TLS; client key material is bundled in the vendor app).
steps.expect: TLS session established with the device.

steps.action: Claim the device to the vendor cloud (only when it reports claim-over-softAP support).
steps.expect: The device acknowledges; the app repeats Wan.Set once a second (up to five sends) until acked.

request.action: Wan.SetHost (type 209: 32-byte broker hostname, then a 1-byte insecure-skip-verify flag), Wan.SetAuthKey (205: 32-byte account token), Wan.Set (202: enable the uplink) — all broadcast-targeted, over the TLS TCP stream

steps.action: Hand over the home network credentials.
steps.expect: No reply is guaranteed; the app re-sends once a second until the device drops the AP to join the home network.

request.action: SetAccessPoint (type 305), interface=STATION(2), ssid, password, security_protocol — the same 98-byte layout as the legacy UDP method, sent over the TLS TCP stream

steps.action: Rejoin the home network and rediscover the device.
steps.expect: The device answers mDNS/UDP discovery on the home LAN; see the discovery block.

timing.resend_interval_notes: The app re-sends the SetAccessPoint request once a second until the device drops the connection (it tears its AP down to join the home network); a disconnect after at least one send is treated as success. The optional cloud-claim Wan.Set is sent up to five times at the same interval until acknowledged.

setup.notes: LIFX strips must be joined to WiFi before the LAN protocol is usable. Unprovisioned (or factory-reset) devices host a temporary AP, and the vendor app — its Wi-Fi protocol layer and onboarding processor — shows TWO onboarding exchanges on it, both speaking the LIFX binary protocol to the device at 172.16.0.1 port 56700 via the access-point message family (304-309) that the original published LAN protocol documented and the current official protocol.yml no longer carries. The modern flow opens a TLS-secured TCP connection to that port; the legacy flow sends the same messages as UDP datagrams. The legacy layouts were first transcribed from the legacy public reverse-engineering documentation (magicmonkey/lifxjs Protocol.md — the same class of source pywemo is for Wemo) and are now confirmed byte-exact against the vendor app; neither flow has been replayed against hardware by this project, hence confidence medium (app-derived, not hardware-verified). During onboarding the app also claims the device to the vendor cloud when the device reports claim-over-softAP support: Wan.SetHost (type 209) hands it the cloud broker hostname, Wan.SetAuthKey (205) a 32-byte account token, and Wan.Set (202) enables the WAN uplink. Matter-firmware units are instead commissioned through the Matter stack the app bundles (see the device notes). Once provisioned, control is unauthenticated UDP and needs no further setup.

rejoin.notes: No documented in-place credential update; treat a router change as a reset-and-reprovision.

discovery_flow: Browse _hap._tcp.local. and keep records where TXT md is LIFX Z.
Use txt:id as the stable MAC/accessory identifier.
Send LIFX LAN GetService message type 2 to UDP port 56700.
lifx_lan_protocol.message_type_notes: set_power 117 is light-level power (LightSetPower); the device-level SetPower message is 21. set_color 102 sets ALL zones at once — per-zone control needs the multizone family below. Full machine-readable message definitions (pkt_type, sizes, fields) are published officially in the LIFX/public-protocol repo (protocol.yml) — the codegen source for a lifx_lan_udp handler. Every type number here, the multizone family below, and the UDP 56700 transport are confirmed byte-exact against the vendor app (its protocol message-type table; its UDP transport sends to port 56700).

get_service.description: Type 2, no payload, sent tagged/broadcast to port 56700; every device answers with a StateService. The example is the exact discovery probe: sequence 0, res_required set.

hsbk.description: The 8-byte colour SetColor/State and the multizone messages carry. Each of hue, saturation and brightness spans the full u16 range (hue as a fraction of 360°); kelvin is 1500..9000 — the white point, meaningful when saturation is 0. Offsets are within the payload that embeds it. Full red is hue 0, saturation and brightness 65535, kelvin 3500.

lan_header.description: The 36-byte header every LIFX LAN message begins with, all little-endian. `protocol` is a bitfield: the low 12 bits are the constant 1024, bit 12 (addressable) is always set, and bit 13 (tagged) is set for a broadcast/discovery message and clear when addressing one device — giving the two constants 0x1400 (addressed) and 0x3400 (tagged/broadcast). `source` is a client-chosen id echoed in replies (this project uses 0x4C425247, "LBRG"). In `response`, bit 0 (res_required) asks the device to answer with its matching State message and bit 1 is ack_required; `sequence` is echoed so a client can correlate that answer.

fields.description: Device MAC in the first 6 bytes (0 for broadcast); last 2 bytes 0.
fields.name: target

set_color.description: LightSetColor, type 102. Payload: one reserved byte, an HSBK colour (see the hsbk format), then `duration` (u32, ms). The example sets the strip to full red, sequence 7, duration 0.

set_color_zones.description: SetColorZones, type 501 (multizone). Payload: start and end zone indices, an HSBK colour, `duration` (u32), and `apply` (1 = apply now, 0 = buffer). The example sets zone 3 to green (hue 21845) and applies it, sequence 4.

set_power.description: LightSetPower, type 117. Payload: `level` (u16, 0 off / 65535 on) then `duration` (u32, milliseconds). The example turns a strip on (target d0:73:d5:aa:bb:cc, sequence 3, duration 0).

state.description: LightState, type 107 — the reply to LightGet (101). Payload: an HSBK colour, two reserved bytes, `power` (u16, 0/65535), a 32-byte UTF-8 label (null-padded), then eight reserved bytes.

state_multi_zone.description: StateMultiZone, type 506 — a reply to GetColorZones (502). Payload: the strip's total zone count, the index this batch starts at, then up to eight HSBK colours (64 bytes). A strip longer than eight zones sends several, keyed by zone index.
